The hand-drawn whiteboard, built so that it keeps to itself.

## ✨ Added

- **Excalidraw, self-hosted, with nothing pointing outward.** The published image runs the app unchanged, and unchanged means it still talks to Excalidraw's own infrastructure: a shared link is stored on their server, a live session keeps its scene in Google Firestore, pasted images go to Firebase Storage, the fonts come from a CDN and an analytics script loads on every visit. None of that is a fault of the project, it is how a free hosted service pays for itself, and all of it is settled when the app is BUILT. This image is that build, done differently: every one of those points back at the container.
- **Shared links and live sessions live in a store of their own.** A small Go binary over SQLite in `/config`, serving the scene, room and file endpoints the app expects. The usual self-hosted answer is a Node service whose published image has not been rebuilt since February 2022; this one is built and tested here, with tests for the round trip, replacing writes, unknown ids, size limits and id randomness.
- **Collaboration runs on your server.** The bundled room server relays between browsers, and the session scene it cannot store is kept by the store above, which is what Firestore was doing.
- **The shape library and text-to-diagram are switches, not decisions.** Both would contact Excalidraw, and both are genuinely useful, so they stay in the build and are turned off by default. `ENABLE_LIBRARY` and `ENABLE_AI` turn either back on; off means the request never leaves your network.
- **HTTPS out of the box**, with a certificate generated on first start and kept in `/config`. This is not decoration: live collaboration needs `crypto.subtle`, which browsers only provide over a secure connection, so on plain HTTP the session button dies with a cryptography error.
- **A gate in the build, not a promise in the README.** After the app is compiled, the build searches it for every address that should be gone and fails if one is left. It also checks that the two switchable addresses are still PRESENT, because a rename upstream would leave the switches pointing at nothing while the container quietly called home.
- **Nothing to configure.** The addresses inside the app are relative paths rather than an absolute URL assembled from a variable you have to set, so the same image works on a LAN address, behind a reverse proxy and under a subdomain without being told which one it is.
- **Unraid template** with both ports, the `/config` share and the two switches, plus a multi-arch image on GHCR and Docker Hub.
